title: Emergence of drifted diffusion in quantum walks with subspace restart
authors: Liwei Qiao, Ruoyu Yin, Wei Zhang
abstract: Restart of a quantum process is typically modeled as a global reinitialization that erases the system's entire history. Here we introduce subspace restart, a protocol that periodically resets only the internal degrees of freedom while preserving the spatial distribution, as a tunable knob for the quantum-to-classical crossover. Using the discrete-time quantum walk as an example, we show that this selective reset drives the walker into an engineered drifted-diffusion regime. This phenomenon can be understood by a Huygens-Fresnel mechanism, where each restart fragments the wave function into a set of independent secondary sources to screen long-range correlations and isolate a robust classical backbone, whose drift and diffusivity are set by the geometric orientation of the initial coin and the restart period. Residual quantum interference, confined to effective light cones, survives only as a short-range correction that renormalizes these coefficients and imprints periodic modulations on the cumulants. Our results establish subspace restart as a route to controlling the quantum-to-classical crossover in synthetic lattices.
summary: The paper introduces 'subspace restart,' a novel periodic reset mechanism for quantum walks that selectively erases history while preserving spatial location. This process forces the walker's dynamics into a predictable drifted-diffusion regime, allowing researchers to engineer transport coefficients like drift and diffusivity with high control. It provides a powerful tool for studying and controlling the fundamental crossover from coherent quantum mechanics to classical diffusion.
main_problem: The paper addresses how to control the transition from quantum wave-like transport to classical diffusive behavior in quantum walks.
main_result: Subspace restart drives the quantum walk into an engineered drifted-diffusion regime, allowing precise tuning of both drift and diffusivity coefficients.
method: The analysis uses a source picture decomposition (Huygens-Fresnel mechanism) to separate the robust classical backbone from residual short-range quantum interference.
model_or_system: The model is a discrete-time quantum walk on an infinite 1D lattice, governed by periodic subspace restarts that reset only the internal coin degrees of freedom while preserving spatial probability.
key_observables: Mean displacement (drift), Mean Squared Displacement ($\langle x^2(n) angle$), effective drift velocity ($v_{	ext{deff}}$), and diffusion coefficient ($D_{	ext{eff}}$).
important_parameters: The restart period ($r$) acts as a tunable knob, controlling the degree of classicalization; the initial coin orientation sets the geometric bias.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations, particularly treating the incoherent sum of source intensities (diagonal approximation), which is valid in certain limits.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the probability distribution $P_r(x, n)$ for different restart periods ($r=1$ vs. $r=25$), showing a clean Gaussian core overlaid with short-range interference fringes, and plot the accumulation of statistical quantities like $\sigma_n^2$ over time steps.
paper_structure: The paper introduces subspace restart as a mechanism to control quantum-to-classical crossover in DTQWs. It develops the source picture description, analyzes the asymptotic Gaussian behavior (incoherent sum), and derives explicit formulas for the effective drift and diffusion coefficients based on the restart period $r$.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, tunable protocol—subspace restart—to engineer macroscopic transport properties in quantum systems, offering an analogy to controlled decoherence or measurement-induced localization relevant to open quantum systems.

(Top) Temporal evolution: unin- terrupted unitary dynamics ˆ W r are interleaved with instan- taneous coin resets R (dashed boxes). (Bottom) Action of R in real space: the spatial probability profile is left invariant, while the internal coin state at every lattice site (blue spheres) is reset from the evolved |φ⟩back to the initial |φ0⟩.

FIG. 2. Occupation probability Pr(x, n) at n = 5000 steps for restart periods (a) r = 1 and (b) r = 25, with three coin orientations (Bloch spheres): left drift (θ, ϕ) = (3π/4, 2π/3) (blue), symmetric spreading (π/2, π/2) (orange), and right drift (π/4, π/3) (green). At r = 1 the distribution is a clean Gaussian, while at r = 25 a Gaussian envelope persists but is dressed by short-range interference fringes, signaling that the macroscopic transport classicalizes while local quantum coherence survives within each cycle. Without specification, only lattice sites with nonzero probability are shown.

FIG. 4. Long-time effective transport coefficients versus restart period r, defined as vdeff = [µRr −µ(R−1)r]/r and Deff = [σ2 Rr −σ2 (R−1)r]/2r, for three coin states: (θ, ϕ) = (π/2, π/2) (yellow triangles), (π/3, π/2) (red circles), and (0, 0) (blue squares). At r = 1, the dynamics reduces to a clas- sical random walk; for r > 1, vdeff saturates to coin-dependent values, while Deff grows linearly with r. Thus subspace restart engineers emergent drifted diffusion in DTQWs.
